prompt: Which of these is a unit test of boxoffice?
hint: One small piece, on its own, with nothing else running.

choices.text: Posting the booking form with curl and reading the total
choices.why: That crosses the server, the form and the page: integration.

choices.text: Booking in a browser on a phone
choices.why: The whole application as a user meets it: a system test.

choices.text: Calling discount for a student with one ticket and checking for 50
choices.why: Right: one function, called directly, with no server.

choices.text: The manager selling two tickets to a student during her afternoon session
choices.why: That is acceptance: the client doing real work.

prompt: Match each layer to its example on boxoffice.
hint: Four layers, from one function up to the client.

pairs.right: A person booking in a real browser

right_distractors: A developer reading discount for mistakes

prompt: By the rule in this lesson, where does the check "a student pays half" belong first?
hint: The cheapest place that can see it.

choices.text: In a unit test of discount
choices.why: Right: it is a rule inside one function, and that is the lowest layer that sees it.

choices.text: In a browser test, since the customer sees the browser
choices.why: The browser test is the slowest and the vaguest when it fails; it comes later, for what only it can see.

choices.text: In UAT, because the client wrote the rule
choices.why: The client accepts the rule; holding it on every change is a job for a faster layer.

choices.text: In all four layers equally, to be safe
choices.why: Repeating the same check at every layer costs the most and adds the least.

prompt: Rui says his unit tests run every row of the discount table on every change. What should that change in your manual testing of prices?
hint: What can those tests not see?

choices.text: Stop testing prices by hand altogether, and test something else
choices.why: The unit tests stop at discount; the form, the page and the total are still untested by them.

choices.text: Run the whole table again by hand, to make sure his tests are right
choices.why: That repeats what a machine already does every change.

choices.text: Nothing: unit tests are the developers' business
choices.why: What they cover is exactly what tells you where your time goes.

choices.text: Spend it where they cannot see: the form and the order page
choices.why: Right: the joins and the screen are left for the upper layers, and for you.

prompt: What does test_discount.py need in order to run?
hint: Compare it with the integration test.

choices.text: boxoffice running in another terminal
choices.why: The integration test needs that; this one calls the function directly.

choices.text: Python, and boxoffice.py in the same directory
choices.why: Right: it imports one function and calls it, with nothing else running.

choices.text: A browser open at the booking page
choices.why: Nothing in it touches a page.

choices.text: A connection to the internet, to download unittest
choices.why: unittest ships with Python.

prompt: unittest runs each method of the class whose name begins with ___.
hint: Look at the five method names.

prompt: Run against version 1.0, test_member_and_five would have failed. What percentage would discount have returned in that test?
hint: In 1.0 the member's discount and the group's were added.

prompt: The unit test reports 0 != 50 for a student. What does it tell the developer that lesson 10's report from the browser could not?
hint: Symptom or cause?

choices.text: That a student is charged the wrong total on the order page
choices.why: That is the symptom, and lesson 10 already showed it.

choices.text: That the form sends the student box under the wrong name
choices.why: A unit test never sees the form.

choices.text: That the cause is inside discount, which ignores its student argument
choices.why: Right: the failing call points at one function, and the code shows why.

choices.text: That the defect only happens with a single ticket
choices.why: The test used one ticket; nothing in it says other quantities are fine.

prompt: After a fix, all five tests in test_discount.py pass, and a student still pays full price on the order page. Which explanation fits?
hint: Where does a unit test stop?

choices.text: The unit tests must be wrong, since they passed
choices.why: They can be right about discount and still not cover the path to it.

choices.text: The tick is lost somewhere on the way from the form
choices.why: Right: a join the unit test never crosses, which an integration test or a browser would show.

choices.text: unittest kept the results of the run before the fix
choices.why: It runs the code afresh every time.

choices.text: The fix only covers orders of one ticket
choices.why: Possible in principle, and nothing about the page explains it better than the join.

prompt: test_booking ends with ERROR and "Connection refused". What happened?
hint: ERROR, not FAIL.

choices.text: Nothing was listening on port 8000
choices.why: Right: boxoffice was not running, so the test never got an answer.

choices.text: boxoffice answered with the wrong total for the student
choices.why: A wrong answer is a FAIL, with the two values shown.

choices.text: The student regression broke the booking form
choices.why: The regression changes a total; it does not refuse connections.

choices.text: test_booking.py has a typing mistake in it
choices.why: A typo in the file would stop it before any test ran.

prompt: Should the two ERRORs from running test_booking with boxoffice stopped go into a defect report against boxoffice?
hint: Did the code under test answer at all?

choices.text: Yes, as two separate defects, one per test
choices.why: There is no defect in boxoffice here at all.

choices.text: Yes, as one defect of high severity
choices.why: Severity is for a fault in the product; this is a fault in the setup.

choices.text: No, because integration tests never find real defects
choices.why: This one found the student regression a minute later.

choices.text: No: the setup failed, and boxoffice itself never answered
choices.why: Right: an ERROR says nothing about boxoffice until the server is running.

prompt: The student regression was seen three times. Match each view to what it shows best.
hint: Cause, cost, and what the customer meets.

pairs.right: What it costs a customer, in reais
What the customer sees on the screen

right_distractors: Whether the client will accept it

prompt: test_booking.py sends student=on itself. Which change could break booking for students and leave test_booking.py green?
hint: What does the test skip that a browser does not?

choices.text: discount ignoring its student argument again
choices.why: The test would catch that: R$ 144,00 is not R$ 80,00.

choices.text: book reading the box under a new name
choices.why: Then student=on is ignored and the total is wrong, so the test fails.

choices.text: The form itself no longer sending the box under that name
choices.why: Right: the test never loads the form, so only a browser would notice.

choices.text: The total being printed with a full stop instead of a comma
choices.why: The test compares "R$ 80,00" exactly, so that fails too.

prompt: Match each test double to what it does.
hint: Answer, conversation, or a simpler working thing.

pairs.right: Gives canned answers and nothing else
Records how it was called, so the test can check the calls
A working, simpler version of the real thing

right_distractors: Replaces the code under test with a copy

prompt: Which kind of test double is boxoffice's outbox?
hint: It works, and takes a shortcut.

choices.text: A stub
choices.why: A stub only hands back canned answers; the outbox keeps and shows every e-mail.

choices.text: A fake
choices.why: Right: a working mail store that never sends anything out.

choices.text: A mock
choices.why: Nothing checks how it was called; it is used, not interrogated.

choices.text: None: it is the real mail server
choices.why: In production the e-mail would leave; in the test build it stops here.

prompt: What does test_signup.py check?
hint: It asks the mock afterwards.

choices.text: That the e-mail reached Caio's real inbox
choices.why: Nothing left the program; the real send never ran.

choices.text: That the outbox shows the confirmation e-mail
choices.why: It checks the opposite: the outbox stayed empty.

choices.text: That the password is between 8 and 64 characters
choices.why: That is signup's rule, and this test is about the e-mail.

choices.text: That signup asked for one e-mail to Caio
choices.why: Right: the conversation between signup and the mail code.

prompt: Why start boxoffice with BOXOFFICE_NOW=2026-10-10T19:30:00-03:00?
hint: R4 talks about an hour before the show.

choices.text: To test the closing rule now, not in the evening
choices.why: Right: the clock is a double, so the test does not wait for the real one.

choices.text: To make the pages answer faster
choices.why: The clock has nothing to do with speed.

choices.text: To clear the orders left by earlier tests
choices.why: A restart does that, whatever the clock says.

choices.text: To make every confirmation link come out the same
choices.why: That is BOXOFFICE_SEED, the third setting of lesson 1.

prompt: Every test of the order page uses a payment stub that always answers "approved". Which defect can none of them find?
hint: What has the stub never said?

choices.text: A total worked out with the wrong discount
choices.why: The stub does not touch the arithmetic, so the tests still see it.

choices.text: Order numbers that skip one after a restart
choices.why: Unrelated to payment; a stub cannot hide it.

choices.text: The page mishandling a declined card
choices.why: Right: a double is a claim, and this one claims no card is ever declined.

choices.text: A student box the form never sends
choices.why: That is about the form, which the stub does not replace.

prompt: Put the steps of testing the closing rule with a fake clock in order.
hint: The setting is read when the program starts.
items: Start it with BOXOFFICE_NOW set to 19:30
Post a booking for The Seagull from the second terminal
Read the message: booking has closed
trap: Changing the variable does nothing to a server already running.

prompt: Suppose book applied the discount twice, so a member paid 81% instead of 90%. Which is the lowest layer that would catch it?
hint: discount itself still returns the right percentage.

choices.text: A unit test of discount
choices.why: discount returns 10, which is right; the mistake is in what book does with it.

choices.text: An integration test, like test_booking.py
choices.why: Right: it reads the total, which is where the second discount shows.

choices.text: Only the client, during the acceptance session
choices.why: A layer far below the client already sees the total.

choices.text: None, short of a person sitting at a browser
choices.why: test_booking.py would fail on the member's R$ 144,00.

prompt: At 10:00 test_booking ends in FAIL: 'R$ 144,00' != 'R$ 80,00'. At 11:00 the same file ends in ERROR: Connection refused. What most likely changed?
hint: ERROR means no answer at all.

choices.text: Rui fixed the student discount
choices.why: A fix would turn the FAIL into ok, not into ERROR.

choices.text: The regression got worse and now crashes the page
choices.why: A crashing page still answers, with a 500; the connection was refused.

choices.text: Somebody edited the expected value in the test
choices.why: An edited expectation still produces ok or FAIL.

choices.text: boxoffice was stopped
choices.why: Right: nothing was listening, so the test could not ask.

prompt: Which of these are test doubles? Choose all that apply.
hint: A stand-in for something real, for the length of a test.

choices.text: The outbox at /outbox
choices.why: Yes: a fake standing in for a mail server.

choices.text: A clock pinned with BOXOFFICE_NOW
choices.why: Yes: a fake clock.

choices.text: test_booking.py
choices.why: It is a test, and it uses the real application.

choices.text: The mock of send in test_signup.py
choices.why: Yes: it records the calls instead of sending.

choices.text: The order page
choices.why: It is the real thing under test.
